title: Safety Footnote Falls Outside the Retrieved Window
summary: The protocol table is retrieved, but the footnote naming the exact subgroup sits in the next chunk. The model answers with a plausible but broader subgroup than the protocol actually specifies.
query: Which Solara trial participants needed weekly liver panels after week 8?

dataset.name: Solara phase II protocol packet
dataset.notes: Synthetic medical-operations corpus with a protocol excerpt, an FAQ, an IRB note, a site memo, and a news brief.

debugChecklist: Inspect whether the answer depends on a footnote or exception attached to a retrieved table row.
If the table looks too broad, check the adjacent chunk for subgroup-specific qualifiers.
When the support spans are adjacent, a parent window or overlap often repairs the failure cleanly.

chunks.label: Protocol chunk 1
chunks.text: Dose reductions are considered after week 8 when ALT rises above grade 2 or the patient enters the rescue schedule.

chunks.label: Protocol chunk 2
chunks.text: Table 4 lists liver panel cadence by subgroup. Standard 100 mg participants move to biweekly panels after week 8.

chunks.label: Protocol chunk 3
chunks.text: Footnote c: participants switched to the 200 mg rescue schedule require weekly liver panels after week 8 even if ALT later stabilizes.

chunks.label: Protocol chunk 4
chunks.text: Investigators should document rescue-schedule status in the safety log before changing panel cadence.

chunks.label: FAQ chunk 1
chunks.text: After week 8, high-risk participants often remain on weekly labs. Standard participants usually move to biweekly monitoring.

chunks.label: IRB chunk 1
chunks.text: The rescue schedule carries the highest monitoring burden because it continues weekly liver panels after week 8.

chunks.label: Site memo chunk 1
chunks.text: Most staff remember that weekly panels belong to the rescue schedule, but the table footnotes should be checked during chart review.

chunks.label: News chunk 1
chunks.text: The Solara study intensified monitoring for some participants after week 8 as dose adjustments increased.
